text: {"features":[{"name":"Baseline qualification fit","description":"How strongly the letter presents the applicant as exceeding the role's baseline academic and software-experience requirements.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter presents only minimum-adjacent preparation, typically a bachelor's-level background with about 3 years of experience and limited production-service scope."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter clearly meets the minimum requirements but shows little preferred-qualification strength beyond them."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows solid baseline fit, such as several years of relevant experience with multiple production launches or one notable preferred qualification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter clearly exceeds the posting on more than one baseline axis, such as advanced academic preparation and 5 or more years of relevant production experience."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents standout baseline strength for this sample, pairing extensive relevant tenure with repeated testing, maintenance, and launch of several production services and strong academic preparation."}]},{"name":"Go depth","description":"The extent to which the letter shows meaningful, role-relevant depth in Go rather than merely listing it.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Go is mentioned only as one item in a language list with no sense of ownership or backend relevance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Go is presented as a working language, but its importance to the applicant's recent work is unclear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Go is described as a principal or regular language in production work, without concrete examples of Go systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Go is framed as the main language for backend or infrastructure systems the applicant built or operated."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Go is positioned as the backbone of substantial security-relevant or agent-supporting backend systems, with clear ownership and direct fit to the role."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"The extent to which the letter demonstrates substantial, production-relevant Python experience.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Python is absent or only vaguely implied."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Python is mentioned as familiarity or occasional scripting, with little sense of depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Python is described as a regular working language for tooling, automation, or services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Python is shown as a daily or production-grade language used across multiple kinds of work, such as services, tooling, analysis, or agents."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Python is presented as a central language for substantial automation, internal services, or agent systems, with clear production ownership."}]},{"name":"AI production depth","description":"How much relevant, production-oriented artificial intelligence experience the letter presents.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No AI or LLM experience is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI interest or exposure without shipped work or concrete responsibilities."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes building or shipping model-backed features, but with limited detail about production demands."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows concrete production AI work with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, or failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents substantial AI experience that is tightly tied to production automation or agent systems and shows mature judgment about safe deployment."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems depth","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates experience designing or operating agentic systems with bounded autonomy.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No agentic systems work is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions automation or AI assistance without actual agent design or bounded autonomy."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states experience with agentic pipelines or agent-based tooling at a high level."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes a clear agent architecture with autonomous Python agents and Go systems providing constraints, permissions, or auditability."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows end-to-end design ownership of agentic systems used for multi-step work, with explicit treatment of autonomy, boundaries, logging, and operational control."}]},{"name":"Security assessment depth","description":"The extent to which the letter shows real experience assessing systems for security risk and following through on findings.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security assessment work is described beyond general security interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter hints at security exposure but does not show concrete assessment practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter mentions conducting reviews, threat models, or assessments at a recognizable level."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes structured assessment work with findings, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation follow-through."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents strong repeated assessment credibility, showing hands-on ownership and a clearly attacker-informed way of examining systems."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability automation depth","description":"How directly and concretely the letter shows experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, or handling workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No vulnerability-handling work is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter expresses interest in reducing security toil but gives no example of prior automation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter mentions automating vulnerability reports or triage at a broad level."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes a concrete workflow with classification, routing, prioritization, deduplication, or similar triage mechanics that reduced manual effort."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents substantial ownership of vulnerability-handling automation as a systems problem, with rich detail about how incoming reports were scaled, routed, or generalized into broader protection."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"The strength of the letter's evidence for data-structure and algorithm skill relevant to systems work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No evidence of data-structure or algorithmic skill is given."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter claims strong fundamentals without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter provides one credible example of using data structures or algorithms to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter gives a clear technical example involving a hot path, brute-force bottleneck, matching problem, graph problem, or similarly nontrivial design choice."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents unusually strong and current algorithmic thinking, with specific examples showing that better structure choice materially changed system performance or tractability."}]},{"name":"Security practice depth","description":"The extent to which the letter shows self-driven security skill-building through certifications, competitions, or other independent practice.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No self-driven security practice is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions light security practice, such as a baseline certification or casual competition participation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows sustained independent investment, such as regular CTF play or a deliberately pursued foundational certification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows high-signal independent security practice, such as OSCP or strong competitive results in CTFs."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents exceptional self-driven security credibility, with serious attacker-style practice and high achievement clearly informing the applicant's engineering perspective."}]},{"name":"Foundational orientation","description":"How strongly the letter shows motivation for platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or users.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives little sense of interest in platform or infrastructure work with broad downstream impact."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions scale or infrastructure in passing but not as a core motivation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly prefers backend or foundational work, though the reasoning is fairly generic."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly ties interest to inherited improvements, cross-organization leverage, or quiet resilience across many systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes foundational impact a central motivation, persuasively framing the role as a chance to strengthen paths that many teams and users rely on."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"How well the letter frames security tooling as a way to help developer teams work safely and efficiently.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not discuss serving other engineers or shaping secure defaults."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows general security interest but little sense of how tooling should help developers."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter mentions reducing manual work or making security easier for engineers in at least one place."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter clearly emphasizes secure-by-default tooling, low-friction workflows, or helping teams rather than policing them."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter strongly presents security engineering as a service discipline that scales expert judgment and makes the right path the easy path for product teams."}]},{"name":"Role tailoring","description":"How specifically the letter is customized to this exact Google Information Security Engineering role rather than to a generic software job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter could be sent to many generic software roles with minimal change."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter names Google or the team but stays mostly generic about fit."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter reflects the broad themes of the posting, such as security automation or backend systems, without much job-specific detail."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter directly addresses several stated responsibilities or preferred qualifications, such as Go back ends, Python agents, vulnerability triage, or security assessments."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates nuanced understanding of this exact role's charter, such as embedding security into the lifecycle, scaling scarce security expertise, or automating variant-style analysis through agentic tooling."}]},{"name":"Evidence specificity","description":"How consistently the letter backs its claims with concrete examples instead of broad assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter relies mostly on broad claims and adjectives with almost no concrete examples."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter includes a few named technologies or tasks but gives little picture of what the applicant actually built or did."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter provides at least one clear project, system, or responsibility as supporting evidence."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter grounds most major claims in concrete projects, technical details, or named responsibilities."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently supports claims with specific systems, technical choices, and circumstances so the reader can readily picture the work performed."}]},{"name":"Impact articulation","description":"How clearly the letter explains the practical effect of the applicant's work on teams, workflows, or systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter describes activities without explaining what changed because of them."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter implies usefulness but gives little concrete sense of effect on people or systems."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter names at least one clear result, such as reduced manual work or removal of a bottleneck."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter connects multiple examples to operational or team impact, such as safer deployments, routed queues, faster paths, or returned expert time."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly translates technical work into clear leverage for teams or systems, making the value of the applicant's contributions easy to grasp."}]},{"name":"Operational rigor","description":"How strongly the letter conveys a mindset of correctness, reliability, guardrails, and careful deployment.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no real signal of correctness, reliability, guardrails, or careful deployment thinking."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter uses generic language about quality or seriousness without operational detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter mentions reliability, correctness, boundaries, testing, or safe deployment in a limited way."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly highlights dependable systems, guardrails, auditability, typed or tested code, evaluation, or clear operational boundaries."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes rigorous safe engineering a core theme and connects that rigor directly to building security tooling or AI systems responsibly."}]},{"name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"The extent to which the letter shows meaningful public-code maintenance or contribution experience.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source activity is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions occasional upstream fixes or lightweight contribution."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows ongoing contribution to external projects or maintenance of a small public project."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter presents active maintenance of a public library or project with recurring reviews, releases, or external use."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial stewardship of an open-source project with a real user or contributor community, making it a meaningful part of the applicant's engineering identity."}]},{"name":"Personal project rigor","description":"How much the letter uses personal builds to demonstrate sustained engineering initiative and technical depth.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No personal project is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a small utility or simple app with little technical depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes a completed side project that shows initiative and some engineering care."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter presents a technically ambitious side project with nontrivial systems or reliability challenges."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows sustained, high-rigor personal systems work chosen specifically to tackle hard engineering problems such as failover, consensus, recovery, or delivery guarantees."}]},{"name":"Writing polish","description":"The overall level of mechanical correctness and professional fluency in the prose.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent spelling, grammar, or usage errors distract from professionalism or slow comprehension."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Multiple noticeable errors are present, though the overall meaning remains recoverable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A few errors appear, but the letter stays readable and generally professional."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The prose is clean and controlled with only minor blemishes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The writing is polished, fluent, and virtually error free throughout."}]}]}
